findings.evidence: In harness/claude_account_cli.py, `_request_usage` adds `usage.input_tokens`, `usage.output_tokens`, `usage.cache_read_tokens`, and `usage.cache_write_tokens` whenever the top-level usage block is present. `usage` is not a model name, so these entries do not satisfy the required “model-name-keyed” per-model breakdown. The new helper-model test explicitly asserts these extra entries, thereby encoding behavior contrary to the semantic criterion rather than detecting it.
findings.required_change: Remove the `usage.*` entries from `RequestUsage.details`; keep the top-level counts only in the aggregate RequestUsage fields, and populate details solely with integer count entries keyed by actual names from `modelUsage`. Update the test and documentation/docstring accordingly.
findings.summary: RequestUsage.details contains non-model-keyed top-level usage entries.

summary: The aggregate usage mapping is implemented, but RequestUsage.details violates the contract’s required per-model-only representation by also recording the top-level usage block as a pseudo-model.
